title: refactor(ci): consolidate workflows, upgrade actions & improve caching for faster CI
author: Liam Chen
description: Motivation: CI runtime has regressed and maintenance burden is high with duplicated workflows across repositories. This PR consolidates lint/test/release workflows into reusable templates, upgrades GitHub Actions and Node toolchain, fixes flaky cache keys, and adds smarter concurrency/cancelation to reduce queuing. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce .github/workflows/ci.yaml as a reusable workflow that covers lint/test/build and is called by language-specific workflow wrappers. 2) Replace deprecated actions and bump to actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4; migrate cache keys to include matrix hashes and lockfile fingerprints. 3) Add job-level concurrency and cancel-in-progress to reduce duplicate runs for rapid pushes. 4) Add build cache layer for TypeScript compilation and yarn/npm install layer (cache + restore). 5) Consolidate release automation into .github/workflows/release.yaml with improved tagging and dry-run support; add manual approval gate for protected branches. 6) Minor repo hygiene: remove legacy .github/workflows/node-legacy.yml and update CONTRIBUTING.md CI docs. Checklist: - [x] Reusable workflows implemented - [x] Actions upgraded and tested - [x] Cache keys validated locally - [x] All tests passing on CI - [x] Docs updated (CONTRIBUTING.md) Rollout plan: merged to main, monitor CI queue times and cache hit rates for one week, revert or hotfix if regressions observed.
commits: fix(ci): improve cache keys to include lockfile and matrix fingerprints
chore(release): consolidate release workflow and add dry-run/approval
review_comments: Ava Patel: Nice consolidation. One request: include lockfile fingerprint in cache key to avoid poisoned cache — addressed in second commit.

Sophia Martinez: Could we add a small matrix exclusion for macOS on lint to reduce queue load? I suggested excluding macOS for lint-only jobs — resolved by moving lint to ubuntu-only in reusable workflow.
Ethan Brooks: Release workflow LGTM but add a manual approval step before publish to npm for protected branches — added approval job and docs note.
Liam Chen (author): Thanks all — addressed comments and pushed fixes; verified cache hits on a follow-up run.
CI Bot: Unit tests failed on first run (integration flaky), re-run and passed.
notes: This is a non-breaking CI refactor that does not affect runtime behavior of any service. Expected impact: ~30% reduction in average CI queue time for pushes and ~45% faster PR turnaround for lint+unit test jobs due to cache improvements and cancel-in-progress. Monitor: ci/queue_time and ci/cache_hit_ratio dashboards.
release_notes:
- Consolidated CI workflows into reusable templates
- Upgraded GitHub Actions to latest stable versions
- Improved caching for faster installs and builds
- Added concurrency/cancel-in-progress to reduce duplicate runs
- Consolidated release workflow with manual approval for protected branches
notes_short: CI workflows consolidated; actions upgraded; cache improvements; release automation refined.
security_notes: Upgraded actions to patched major versions and added a security-scan step. No secrets or tokens introduced. Release workflow uses protected branch approval.
incident_reference: PR originated from triage of CI regression reported in ENG-1234; no user-facing incident.
